wave: TRUST BOUNDARY -- manifest-declared source roots cannot escape the repository workspace
wave_title: adapter::source::inventory_declared_source joined each of manifest.source_roots/backend_roots/frontend_roots/test_roots against the repository root with a bare Path::join and walked the result with no containment check. An absolute declared root (Path::join returns an absolute joinee verbatim, discarding the intended root) or a `..`-escaping declared root could cause a full filesystem walk and file-content read outside the intended repository boundary, and core::constraint::validate_manifest never inspected these four array fields at all, so nothing at the policy layer would have caught it either.

generation_model.G_n: 0f4735e0be (fix(runtime): gate coding_admission on constraint_results, not just diagnostics) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Moved from priority-1 (correctness, closed for this pass in the ADL compiler) to priority-2 (security/trust boundary) per the standing loop's own priority order, an area not yet audited this session. Delegated a scoped investigation (Explore agent) for path-traversal, untrusted-input-to-dangerous-sink, and subprocess-injection patterns across core/src, runtime/src, adapter/src, apps/cli/src, excluding the files already hardened this session. It found and reported the manifest-declared-root traversal gap with file:line precision, citing `.atlas/contracts/EXTERNAL-PROVIDER-TRUST.md`'s 'Capability minimum' clause forbidding 'arbitrary filesystem outside assigned workspace' as the violated rule. Independently verified every claim directly against the code before acting: confirmed `relative()`'s `strip_prefix(root).unwrap_or(path)` silently falls back to the raw (possibly absolute/escaping) path when containment fails (adapter/src/source/mod.rs), confirmed `validate_manifest` (core/src/constraint/mod.rs) never inspects the four root-array fields, and additionally discovered (beyond what the agent reported) that `audit_repository` sets `manifest: Some(parsed)` unconditionally on successful parse -- even when `policy_violations` is non-empty -- and that `runtime::systemize`/`graph`/`code_analyze` all call `inventory_declared_source` directly whenever a manifest exists, with no gate on `repository.ready`/`policy_violations` before doing so. This meant a policy-layer-only fix would have been silently bypassed in practice: the actual filesystem walk (the sink) had to be the primary enforcement point, not only the manifest-validation report.

priority_classification: security/trust boundary (priority 2). `.atlas/contracts/EXTERNAL-PROVIDER-TRUST.md`'s 'Capability minimum' section requires default-deny on 'arbitrary filesystem outside assigned workspace' for every provider invocation, and its own candidate-reconciliation path (`ADL-TO-ATLAS.md`) plus this session's own donor-corpus census sweeps against externally-authored trees are concrete, already-established mechanisms by which `inventory_declared_source` can be pointed at a `.atlas/repo.toml` this session did not author.

design_decisions.question: Detect the escape via `canonicalize()`-and-compare, or purely lexically?
design_decisions.decision: Purely lexically (component-by-component `..`-depth tracking, reject any absolute path outright). `canonicalize()` requires the path to exist and itself follows symlinks/`..` against the real filesystem -- calling it on an attacker-influenced path is closer to the sink we are trying to guard, not a safe way to guard it, and a declared root legitimately may not exist yet (the pre-existing 'declared root doesn't exist' case is already silently skipped downstream). A lexical check needs no filesystem access at all and cannot itself be tricked by symlinks.

design_decisions.question: Enforce only at the policy layer (`validate_manifest`), only at the sink (`inventory_declared_source`), or both?
design_decisions.decision: Both, but the sink-side check is load-bearing and the policy-side check is reporting/defense-in-depth. Investigation confirmed `runtime::systemize`/`graph`/`code_analyze` never gate inventory-building on `repository.ready`/`policy_violations` -- they call `inventory_declared_source` for any manifest that successfully *parsed*, regardless of policy_violations. A policy-only fix would report the escape as a blocker (`REPO_GATE_NOT_READY`) but the unsafe walk would already have happened by the time that blocker is inspected. `core` has no dependency on `adapter` (workspace layering), so the lexical check is duplicated as two small (~15-line), independently-tested pure functions rather than introducing a new shared-utility crate for one function -- consistent with this codebase's existing preference for small extracted pure predicates over cross-crate coupling.

design_decisions.question: Silently drop a rejected declared root, or record it?
design_decisions.decision: Record it, as an `ArtifactRecord` with `disposition: IgnoredByExplicitPolicy` and `reason: "declared-root-escapes-repository-boundary"` -- the exact same disposition already used for `policy_boundary()` (ignored directories like `.git`/`node_modules`), so it participates correctly in existing `InventoryReport::is_closed()` accounting rather than being an untracked exception. Silently dropping with no signal at all would repeat the precise silent-fallback pattern this session already found and fixed twice in the ADL compiler this same session (unrecognized constraint syntax; invariants never evaluated) -- a third instance of 'unhandled input defaults to invisible' was avoidable by design, not merely by inspection.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: A manifest-declared root that is absolute, or whose `..` components net-escape above the repository root, is never walked by `inventory_declared_source` (the sink) regardless of whether `validate_manifest` ran or passed, and is separately reported as a `policy_violations` entry (and therefore blocks `REPO_GATE_NOT_READY`) when it does run. An ordinary relative declared root continues to be walked exactly as before, with zero behavioral change.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: core/src/constraint/mod.rs: 5 new tests (ordinary_relative_roots_are_contained, an_absolute_root_is_never_contained, a_net_upward_traversal_is_never_contained, validate_manifest_reports_an_escaping_source_root_as_a_violation, validate_manifest_accepts_ordinary_relative_roots). adapter/src/source/mod.rs: 3 new tests, the load-bearing ones -- a_declared_root_escaping_via_dotdot_is_rejected_not_walked (constructs a real sibling directory on disk with a real file inside it, declares a `../`-escaping root pointing at it, and asserts the resulting InventoryReport contains no artifact referencing that file, proving the walk genuinely never happened, not merely that a check function returns the right boolean in isolation), a_declared_root_that_is_an_absolute_path_is_rejected_not_walked, an_ordinary_declared_root_is_still_walked_normally (regression guard).
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: Re-ran `atlas-cli systemize --root .` against this repository's own real `.atlas/repo.toml` (not a synthetic fixture): `repository.ready: true`, `repository.policy_violations: []`, `coding_admission` blockers unchanged from the prior generation (still only the pre-existing, unrelated `ADL_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATED`/WebUI gap) -- proving the new containment check does not misclassify this repository's own real, legitimate, all-relative declared roots (`source_roots = ["core"]`, etc.) as escaping.

implementation.sink_enforcement: adapter/src/source/mod.rs -- new pure fn declared_root_is_contained(&str) -> bool (lexical, no filesystem access); new fn rejected_declared_root(&str) -> ArtifactRecord (IgnoredByExplicitPolicy); inventory_declared_source now partitions declared roots into walked vs. rejected before ever constructing a joined PathBuf that gets passed to inventory_from_roots, and merges rejected records back into the final InventoryReport
implementation.policy_enforcement: core/src/constraint/mod.rs -- new pure fn declared_root_is_contained(&str) -> bool (independent copy, core has no adapter dependency); validate_manifest now checks all four root-array fields (source_roots, backend_roots, frontend_roots, test_roots) and reports a violation per escaping entry

the same investigation ruled out (with specific evidence, not merely absence of search) other priority-2 candidates: no production subprocess invocation is influenced by untrusted content (the only two Command::new sites are a #[cfg(test)]-only cargo-metadata oracle, already excluded from the production build, and a git invocation using a fixed literal argv with no shell interpolation); no production code deserializes untrusted JSON into a behavior-driving type; there is no unsafe code in core/adapter/runtime/apps. These are recorded here as ruled-out, not re-investigated, so a future generation does not re-spend effort re-confirming them without new information.

the same 'sink enforcement must not depend on an upstream gate that isn't actually wired to block execution' lesson (policy_violations existing does not mean anything actually checks it before acting) is worth keeping in mind when auditing other gates in this codebase -- this generation found one concrete instance (repository.ready/policy_violations vs. inventory-building) beyond what the delegated investigation itself surfaced
overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED AND VERIFIED. Closes a real path-traversal / workspace-escape trust-boundary defect: a manifest-declared source root that was absolute or net-upward-`..`-escaping could previously cause a full filesystem walk and file-content read outside the intended repository boundary, with no defense at either the sink (adapter::source::inventory_declared_source) or the policy layer (core::constraint::validate_manifest) -- and critically, the policy layer alone would not have been sufficient, since runtime::systemize/graph/code_analyze do not gate inventory-building on policy_violations passing. Both layers now enforce the same lexical containment rule independently. Verified with a real-filesystem exploit-scenario test (a real file outside the root, confirmed absent from the resulting inventory) and against this repository's own real, unaffected manifest.
